name: Debugging and Problem Solving
description: Finding and fixing faults methodically: hypothesis-led method, reproduction, isolation, debugger and log tools, common and concurrent bug classes, performance and production debugging, web and network tools, cognitive pitfalls and prevention.

cards.subject: Scientific method
says: forms a hypothesis about the cause and tests it with an experiment
changes one thing at a time so each result can be explained
cards.use: need to find a cause instead of guessing
not: rewrites code until the symptom disappears

cards.subject: Shotgun debugging
says: makes many unrelated changes at once hoping one of them fixes the fault
leaves the team unsure which change mattered
cards.use: feel tempted to change several things at once
not: is the fastest reliable way to find a cause

cards.subject: Rubber duck debugging
says: explains the code line by line to an inanimate listener
exposes a wrong assumption by forcing it to be said aloud
cards.use: are stuck and have nobody to ask

cards.subject: Five whys
says: asks why repeatedly to move from a symptom to a root cause
stops at a cause the team can actually change
cards.use: want to look past the first obvious cause of an incident
not: names the person who made the mistake

cards.subject: Root cause
says: is the underlying defect whose removal stops the failure recurring
often lies in a different place from where the failure appears
cards.use: need to know whether a fix is complete

cards.subject: Symptom
says: is the visible failure that users or tests first notice
may be several steps away from the defect that produced it
cards.use: are describing what a user saw rather than why

cards.subject: Hypothesis falsification
says: designs a test that could prove the current guess wrong
prefers disconfirming evidence over repeating runs that agree with the theory
cards.use: have a theory that every run so far seems to support

cards.subject: Assumption audit
says: lists what is believed to be true and checks each belief in turn
finds a bug hiding in something nobody thought to question
cards.use: have checked everything you thought could be wrong

cards.subject: Working backwards
says: starts from the first wrong output and traces back to where it became wrong
suits a failure with a clear bad value in the result
cards.use: can see exactly which output is incorrect

cards.subject: Checking recent changes
says: asks what changed since the system last worked
finds most regressions faster than reading old code
cards.use: hear that something worked yesterday and is broken today

cards.subject: Minimal reproducible example
says: strips a failure down to the smallest code that still shows it
lets someone else run the failure without the full application
cards.use: need to report a bug to a library maintainer
not: copies the whole repository into the report

cards.subject: Steps to reproduce
says: lists the exact actions that trigger the failure in order
states the expected result beside the actual result
cards.use: write a bug report for a tester

cards.subject: Environment capture
says: records versions, configuration and operating system of the failing run
explains why a bug appears on one machine only
cards.use: hear it works on my machine

cards.subject: Record and replay
says: records a run so the same execution can be replayed deterministically
lets a developer step backwards through a failure that happened once
cards.use: must investigate a failure that has happened only once

cards.subject: Fixed random seed
says: makes a randomised test produce the same inputs on every run
lets a flaky failure be rerun exactly
cards.use: have a test that fails on some random inputs

cards.subject: Failing test first
says: turns the reproduction into an automated test that fails before the fix
proves afterwards that the fix works
cards.use: have just reproduced a bug by hand

cards.subject: Anonymised production sample
says: uses a scrubbed copy of real records to recreate a data-dependent bug
avoids copying personal data into development
cards.use: cannot reproduce a bug with the test data you have
not: copies customer records unchanged into a laptop

cards.subject: Clock control
says: freezes or injects time so date-dependent bugs can be reproduced
exposes failures at month ends, leap days and time-zone changes
cards.use: see failures only around midnight or month end

cards.subject: Flaky test quarantine
says: isolates a non-deterministic test so it stops blocking the pipeline
keeps the test and a ticket so the cause still gets fixed
cards.use: have a test that fails one run in twenty
not: deletes the test to keep the build green

cards.subject: Binary search debugging
says: halves the suspect area with each check
finds a faulty step among many in a logarithmic number of checks
cards.use: have a long process and no idea which step breaks it

cards.subject: Git bisect
says: searches commit history for the change that introduced a bug
needs one known good commit and one known bad commit
cards.use: know it worked last month and is broken now

cards.subject: Delta debugging
says: automatically shrinks a failing input to a minimal one
repeatedly removes parts of the input while the failure persists
cards.use: have a huge input that crashes a parser

cards.subject: Divide the pipeline
says: checks the data at the boundary between two stages
decides which side of the boundary holds the fault
cards.use: have data passing through several stages and a wrong result at the end

cards.subject: Stubbing a dependency
says: replaces a collaborator with a fixed fake to rule it out
shows whether the fault lies inside or outside the unit
cards.use: suspect a downstream service but cannot prove it

cards.subject: Feature flag toggle
says: switches a suspect feature off in a running system to test whether it is the cause
is quicker than redeploying older code
cards.use: suspect one new feature of causing errors in production

cards.subject: Differential comparison
says: compares a working case with a failing one to spot what differs
covers inputs, configuration and environment
cards.use: have one request that works and a similar one that fails

cards.subject: Configuration diff
says: compares settings between a healthy and a broken environment
finds a setting that was changed by hand
cards.use: have staging working and production failing

cards.subject: Rollback as diagnosis
says: reverts to the last known good release to confirm the release is the cause
restores service while the investigation continues
cards.use: see errors begin right after a deployment

cards.subject: Breakpoint
says: pauses execution at a chosen line
lets variables be inspected at that moment
cards.use: want to see program state at one point in the code

cards.subject: Conditional breakpoint
says: pauses only when an expression is true
avoids stopping on every iteration of a loop
cards.use: need to stop on the one bad item among thousands

cards.subject: Step over
says: runs the current line including any function it calls and then pauses
skips the detail of called functions
cards.use: trust the function on the current line and want to move on

cards.subject: Step into
says: enters the function called on the current line
lets you follow execution into a callee
cards.use: suspect the function on the current line is wrong

cards.subject: Watchpoint
says: pauses when a chosen variable or memory location changes
finds the line that corrupts a value
cards.use: know which value is wrong but not which code changes it

cards.subject: Call stack
says: lists the chain of function calls that led to the current point
shows who called the function that is running
cards.use: are paused in a function and need to know how you got there

cards.subject: Stack trace
says: prints the call chain at the moment an error was raised
points to the line where the exception originated
cards.use: read an error report from a crashed program

cards.subject: Core dump
says: saves the memory image of a crashed process for later analysis
allows a crash to be examined after the process has gone
cards.use: need to analyse a crash that happened on a server you cannot attach to

cards.subject: Address sanitizer
says: instruments code to detect out-of-bounds and use-after-free access at run time
reports the exact allocation involved in a memory error
cards.use: suspect memory corruption in native code

cards.subject: Log level
says: separates debug detail from errors by severity
lets verbosity be raised without changing code
cards.use: want detailed output only while investigating

cards.subject: Structured logging
says: writes log entries as key-value fields instead of free text
makes entries searchable by field
cards.use: need to filter millions of log lines by user or order

cards.subject: Correlation ID
says: is a unique identifier passed through every service that handles a request
lets one request's log lines be joined across services
cards.use: must follow one request through several services

cards.subject: Distributed trace
says: records the timed path of one request across services
shows which hop added the delay
cards.use: know a request is slow but not which service is responsible

cards.subject: Metric
says: is a numeric measurement sampled over time
shows trends such as error rate and latency
cards.use: want to see whether a problem is growing

cards.subject: Log sampling
says: keeps only a fraction of high-volume log entries
controls cost while keeping representative detail
cards.use: have log volume that is too expensive to store in full

cards.subject: Sensitive data redaction
says: removes passwords, tokens and personal data before logs are written
keeps logs safe to share with support
cards.use: must send logs to a vendor or another team

cards.subject: Symptom-based alerting
says: pages on user-visible failure such as error rate rather than on every internal cause
reduces noise that trains people to ignore alerts
cards.use: are woken by alerts that turn out to need no action

cards.subject: Observability
says: lets you ask new questions about system behaviour from the data it emits
goes beyond checking dashboards built for known failures
cards.use: face a failure nobody predicted when the dashboards were built

cards.subject: Off-by-one error
says: miscounts a loop or index boundary by exactly one
reads one element too many or too few
cards.use: see the first or last item skipped or an index out of range

cards.subject: Null reference
says: uses a value that was never set
raises an error when a member of nothing is accessed
cards.use: see a crash on a missing value

cards.subject: Integer overflow
says: exceeds the largest value a numeric type can hold
turns a large positive number negative in fixed-width types
cards.use: see a counter or total suddenly become negative

cards.subject: Floating-point rounding
says: gives 0.1 plus 0.2 a result slightly different from 0.3
makes exact equality checks on decimals unreliable
cards.use: compare computed money or measurement values for equality

cards.subject: Use after free
says: reads memory after it has been returned to the allocator
produces corrupted data or exploitable crashes
cards.use: see random crashes in native code that move when the code changes

cards.subject: Stale cache
says: serves an old copy after the source has changed
disappears when the cache is cleared
cards.use: see old data until someone clears something

cards.subject: Time zone error
says: mixes local time and UTC
shows a one-hour or whole-day shift in stored dates
cards.use: see dates a day out for users in some countries

cards.subject: Encoding error
says: decodes bytes with the wrong character set
turns accented characters into garbage
cards.use: see accented names corrupted after an import

cards.subject: Heisenbug
says: changes or disappears when you try to observe it
is often hidden by added logging or a debugger
cards.use: find a failure that stops when you attach the debugger

cards.subject: Race condition
says: gives different outcomes depending on the timing of threads or requests
arises when shared state is changed without coordination
cards.use: see results that differ between identical runs under load

cards.subject: Deadlock
says: leaves two or more tasks each waiting for a lock the other holds
stops progress with no error raised
cards.use: see a system hang with no CPU use and no errors

cards.subject: Livelock
says: keeps tasks busy reacting to each other without making progress
differs from deadlock because the tasks are not blocked
cards.use: see high CPU use but no work completing

cards.subject: Starvation
says: prevents one task from ever getting the resource it needs
happens when other tasks always take priority
cards.use: see one low-priority job never finishing

cards.subject: Mutex
says: allows only one thread into a critical section at a time
protects shared data from simultaneous change
cards.use: need exclusive access to shared data

cards.subject: Lost update
says: overwrites another writer's change after both read the same old value
is prevented by optimistic locking or atomic updates
cards.use: see two users save at once and one edit vanish

cards.subject: Thread dump
says: lists what every thread is doing and holding at one instant
reveals which threads are blocked on which locks
cards.use: must diagnose a hung process

cards.subject: Thread sanitizer
says: detects unsynchronised access to shared memory at run time
reports data races even when no failure occurred
cards.use: suspect a data race but cannot make it fail

cards.subject: Lock ordering
says: acquires multiple locks in one agreed sequence
removes the circular wait that causes deadlock
cards.use: need code to take two locks safely

cards.subject: Profiler
says: measures where a program spends its time
shows the functions that dominate run time
cards.use: want to know why a program is slow
not: guesses the slow function from reading the code

cards.subject: Flame graph
says: stacks sampled call stacks so width shows share of time
makes the hottest code path visible at a glance
cards.use: need to read thousands of profile samples quickly

cards.subject: Baseline measurement
says: records performance before any change
makes it possible to prove an improvement
cards.use: are about to optimise something

cards.subject: N+1 query
says: runs one extra query per row after an initial list query
shows up as hundreds of near-identical queries for one page
cards.use: see a page slow down as the list grows

cards.subject: Query plan
says: shows how the database will execute a query
reveals a full table scan where an index was expected
cards.use: have a query that is slow on a large table

cards.subject: Percentile latency
says: reports the time within which a given share of requests finish
exposes a slow tail that an average hides
cards.use: hear that the average response time looks fine but users complain

cards.subject: Amdahl's law
says: limits overall speed-up by the part that cannot be improved
shows why optimising a small hotspot gains little
cards.use: wonder how much faster the whole system gets from tuning one part

cards.subject: Premature optimisation
says: tunes code before measurement shows a problem
spends effort on code that is not the bottleneck
cards.use: are tempted to rewrite code for speed without data

cards.subject: Load test
says: applies realistic demand to find limits before users do
reveals failures that only appear under volume
cards.use: must know whether a release will cope with launch traffic

cards.subject: Rollback
says: returns to the previous release when the new one misbehaves
restores service faster than a fix forward
cards.use: see a release cause errors and a fix is not ready

cards.subject: Canary release
says: sends a small share of traffic to the new version first
limits the damage of a bad release
cards.use: want evidence a release is safe before everyone gets it

cards.subject: Health check
says: reports whether an instance can serve traffic
lets a load balancer stop routing to a failing instance
cards.use: need failing servers removed from rotation automatically

cards.subject: Incident commander
says: coordinates the response and assigns roles during an incident
stops everyone debugging the same thing at once
cards.use: have many people and no clear owner in an outage

cards.subject: Mitigate before diagnose
says: restores service first and finds the root cause afterwards
puts user impact ahead of understanding
cards.use: face an outage while the cause is still unknown

cards.subject: Circuit breaker
says: stops calls to a failing dependency after repeated errors
gives the dependency time to recover and protects callers
cards.use: see one slow dependency drag down every caller

cards.subject: Idempotency key
says: lets a retried request be recognised and applied only once
prevents duplicates when a client retries after a timeout
cards.use: see customers charged twice after a network timeout

cards.subject: Dead-letter queue
says: holds messages that repeatedly failed processing
lets them be inspected and replayed without blocking the queue
cards.use: have one poison message stopping a consumer

cards.subject: Runbook
says: documents the steps to diagnose and fix a known failure
lets the on-call engineer act without its author
cards.use: are paged at night for a failure seen before

cards.subject: Browser inspector
says: inspects the DOM, styles and console of a live page
needs no change to the application code
cards.use: need to see why a page looks or behaves wrongly

cards.subject: Network tab
says: lists every request a page makes with its status and timing
shows failed or slow calls
cards.use: need to see which request fails when a page loads

cards.subject: HTTP status code
says: tells whether a request succeeded, was redirected or failed
separates client errors in the 4xx range from server errors in the 5xx range
cards.use: need to know whether the fault is on the client or the server side

cards.subject: CORS error
says: is raised by the browser when a cross-origin response lacks permission headers
cannot be fixed from client code alone
cards.use: see a call blocked in the browser but working in curl

cards.subject: curl
says: sends a raw HTTP request from the command line
takes the browser out of the equation when testing an endpoint
cards.use: need to know whether an API or the front end is at fault

cards.subject: dig
says: checks which address a name resolves to
explains failures where a host name still points to the old server
cards.use: see traffic reaching the wrong server after a migration

cards.subject: Certificate inspection
says: shows who issued a certificate and when it expires
explains handshake failures after expiry
cards.use: see secure connections fail suddenly with no code change

cards.subject: Intercepting proxy
says: sits between client and server to view and modify traffic
helps debug mobile apps whose requests cannot be seen in a browser
cards.use: need to see the requests a mobile app sends

cards.subject: Source map
says: maps minified code back to the original source
makes production stack traces readable
cards.use: see an error pointing at line 1 of a minified file

cards.subject: Confirmation bias
says: looks only for evidence that supports the current theory
stops other causes being considered
cards.use: keep rerunning tests that agree with your first idea

cards.subject: First-error anchoring
says: treats the first message in a log as the cause
ignores that it may be an effect of an earlier failure
cards.use: are reading a long log full of errors

cards.subject: Blaming the framework
says: suspects the library or compiler before checking own code
is rarely the true cause of a failure
cards.use: are convinced a well-used library has a bug

cards.subject: Fixing the symptom
says: makes the visible failure stop without removing its cause
lets the defect return in another place
cards.use: are tempted to add a check that hides a bad value

cards.subject: Tunnel vision
says: keeps checking the same area after repeated failures
is broken by a break or a fresh pair of eyes
cards.use: have spent hours on one component without progress

cards.subject: Sunk cost
says: continues a failing line of investigation because of time already spent
is cured by setting a time limit
cards.use: are reluctant to abandon a theory after a long investigation

cards.subject: Time boxing
says: sets a limit before asking for help or changing approach
stops hours disappearing into one theory
cards.use: want to avoid being stuck all day on a single idea

cards.subject: Ignoring the error message
says: skips the text that already names the problem
leads to guessing instead of reading
cards.use: have a failure and are about to try random changes

cards.subject: Cargo-cult fix
says: applies a fix found online without understanding why it works
may hide the real problem
cards.use: are about to paste a snippet that made someone else's error go away

cards.subject: Regression test
says: fails if a fixed bug comes back
is written from the reproduction of the bug
cards.use: have just fixed a bug

cards.subject: Code review
says: has a second person examine a change before merge
catches defects the author cannot see
cards.use: want a second opinion before code reaches production

cards.subject: Static analysis
says: inspects code without running it for likely defects
flags issues such as unused variables and possible null use
cards.use: want defects found before the code runs

cards.subject: Assertion
says: stops the program when an impossible condition is detected
brings a failure close to its cause
cards.use: want a wrong assumption to fail loudly

cards.subject: Fail fast
says: reports invalid state as soon as it is detected
stops corrupted data travelling away from where it began
cards.use: want errors to surface near their origin

cards.subject: Property-based testing
says: checks that stated properties hold across generated inputs
finds edge cases a hand-written example would miss
cards.use: want to test a rule that must hold for every input

cards.subject: Fuzzing
says: feeds malformed or random input to find crashes
finds parser and memory-safety bugs
cards.use: need to harden code that parses untrusted input

cards.subject: Blameless postmortem
says: reviews an incident to learn how the system allowed it
avoids naming a person as the cause
cards.use: have just resolved a serious incident
not: assigns the failure to the engineer who deployed

cards.subject: Chaos experiment
says: injects failures deliberately in a controlled way
checks that recovery works before a real outage
cards.use: want evidence a system survives losing a dependency

cards.subject: Mutation testing
says: alters code to see whether tests fail
reveals tests that would not notice a bug
cards.use: suspect a high-coverage suite still misses bugs

qa.q: A loop runs for i from 0 to items.length inclusive and reads items[i]. What is the bug?
qa.right: An off-by-one error causing an out-of-range read
qa.why: The loop bound goes one past the last valid index.

qa.q: Your colleague sees a blank page and you do not. What should you check first?
qa.right: Compare browser, version and console errors between the two machines
qa.why: Finding the difference between working and failing cases is the quickest first step.

qa.q: A bug appeared sometime in the last 200 commits. What is the most efficient way to find the commit?
qa.right: Run git bisect with a known good and a known bad commit
wrong: Revert half the files at random
Ask who last touched the file
qa.why: Bisect finds the commit in about eight checks for 200 commits.

qa.q: A test fails once in twenty runs and blocks every build. What is the best immediate action?
qa.right: Quarantine it with a ticket and keep investigating the cause
wrong: Rerun until green and ignore it
Raise the timeout to one hour
qa.why: Quarantine unblocks the pipeline without losing the signal.

qa.q: A user reports that the app is slow. What do you do before changing any code?
qa.right: Measure to find where the time goes
qa.why: Optimising without measurement often targets the wrong part.

qa.q: A page makes 301 database queries: one for the list and one per row. What is this pattern?
qa.right: An N+1 query problem
qa.why: One query per row after the list query is the N+1 pattern.

qa.q: The average response time is 120 ms but customers complain. Which measure helps most?
qa.right: 99th percentile latency
qa.why: The slow tail is hidden by averages.

qa.q: Two requests update the same record. Both read the same value; one change is lost. What is this?
qa.right: A lost update
qa.why: Both writers started from the same old value.

qa.q: A system hangs with no CPU use and no errors. A thread dump shows two threads each waiting on a lock the other holds. What is this?
qa.right: A deadlock
qa.why: Circular waiting on locks is a deadlock.

qa.q: Threads are busy and CPU is high but no work completes because they keep yielding to each other. What is this?
qa.right: A livelock
qa.why: In a livelock tasks are active but make no progress.

qa.q: Errors began minutes after a deployment and the fix is not yet known. What should you do first?
qa.right: Roll back or switch off the feature to restore service
qa.why: Restoring service comes before understanding the cause.

qa.q: Customers were charged twice after a gateway timeout and client retry. What protects against this?
qa.right: An idempotency key on the payment request
qa.why: The server can recognise the retried request and apply it once.

qa.q: A call works with curl but fails in the browser with a cross-origin message. What is the likely cause?
qa.right: The response lacks the CORS permission headers
qa.why: Browsers enforce CORS; curl does not.

qa.q: Production errors show line 1, column 48210 of a single minified file. What helps?
qa.right: Source maps
qa.why: Source maps translate minified positions into original source.

qa.q: A fix removes the error shown to users by catching the exception and returning an empty list. What is wrong with it?
qa.right: It treats the symptom and hides the cause
wrong: It is always the best practice
qa.why: The defect remains and the data is silently wrong.

qa.q: You have a theory about a bug and every run you try confirms it. What should you do next?
qa.right: Design a test that could prove the theory wrong
qa.why: Confirming runs do not distinguish between theories.

qa.q: After a long outage, a manager asks who is to blame. What is the best response in a blameless postmortem?
qa.right: Describe the conditions that let the failure happen and the actions that prevent it
qa.why: Blameless reviews look at the system rather than individuals.

qa.q: A function returns 0.30000000000000004 for 0.1 + 0.2. Why?
qa.right: Binary floating point cannot represent those decimals exactly
qa.why: Many decimal fractions have no exact binary representation.

qa.q: Names such as José are shown as JosÃ© after an import. What is the likely cause?
qa.right: Bytes decoded with the wrong character set
qa.why: UTF-8 bytes read as Latin-1 produce this pattern.

qa.q: A server's order counter becomes negative after passing 2,147,483,647. What is the likely cause?
qa.right: Integer overflow in a 32-bit signed value
qa.why: A signed 32-bit integer wraps past its maximum.

qa.q: Users in Sydney see yesterday's date for records created in the evening in London. What is likely wrong?
qa.right: Local time and UTC are being mixed
qa.why: Date boundaries differ by zone when stored times are not normalised.

qa.q: A bug disappears when you add a print statement. What kind of bug is it likely to be?
qa.right: A timing-dependent bug such as a race condition
qa.why: Observation changes timing and can hide races.

qa.q: An error log has fifty errors. Which one do you investigate first?
qa.right: The earliest one, since later ones may be consequences
wrong: The one with the most familiar name
qa.why: A first failure often causes the rest.

qa.q: You have spent three hours on one theory without progress. What is best?
qa.right: Step back, list assumptions and ask someone else to look
qa.why: A time box and fresh view break tunnel vision.

qa.q: Where should a correlation ID be generated?
qa.right: At the first service that receives the request, then passed on to every downstream call
qa.why: One shared identifier lets logs be joined.

qa.q: Which log line is most useful for debugging a payment failure?
qa.right: A structured entry with order ID, error code and correlation ID
qa.why: Structured, identifying fields help; card numbers must never be logged.

qa.q: You must send an application log file to a supplier. What do you do first?
qa.right: Check it for tokens, passwords and personal data and redact them
qa.why: Logs often contain secrets that must not leave the organisation.

qa.q: A program uses more memory every hour until it is restarted. What helps most to find the cause?
qa.right: Compare heap snapshots taken at different times
qa.why: The objects that grow between snapshots show what is retained.

qa.q: A query is slow on a large table. What do you look at first?
qa.right: The query plan
wrong: The size of the code file
qa.why: The plan shows whether an index is used.

qa.q: After fixing a bug, what should you add before closing the ticket?
qa.right: A test that fails without the fix
qa.why: A regression test keeps the bug from returning.

qa.q: A parser crashes on malformed uploads from the internet. Which technique finds more such cases?
qa.right: Fuzzing
qa.why: Fuzzing generates unexpected inputs automatically.

qa.q: Test coverage is 95 percent but bugs still escape. Which technique checks whether the tests would notice a change?
qa.right: Mutation testing
qa.why: Mutation testing changes code and checks that tests fail.

qa.q: A service keeps calling a failing dependency and its own threads are exhausted. What pattern helps?
qa.right: A circuit breaker
qa.why: It stops calls to a failing dependency and lets callers fail fast.

qa.q: A message in the queue crashes the consumer every time and blocks the queue. What is the usual answer?
qa.right: Move it to a dead-letter queue after a set number of attempts
qa.why: Dead-letter queues remove poison messages while keeping them for inspection.

qa.q: You are paged for a known failure at night. Which document should exist?
qa.right: A runbook
qa.why: A runbook lets the on-call engineer follow tested steps.

qa.q: Alerts fire every few minutes for brief CPU spikes and people have started ignoring them. What is the best fix?
qa.right: Alert on user-visible symptoms such as error rate
qa.why: Actionable symptom alerts keep trust in paging.

qa.q: Which statement about rubber duck debugging is true?
qa.right: Explaining the problem aloud often reveals a mistaken assumption
wrong: It only works for syntax errors
qa.why: The act of explaining forces each step to be examined.

qa.q: You change three settings at once and the bug disappears. What is the problem?
qa.right: You do not know which change fixed it
qa.why: One change at a time keeps results explainable.

qa.q: A staging environment works and production fails with the same code. What is the best next step?
qa.right: Compare configuration and dependency versions between them
qa.why: Same code and different behaviour points to environment differences.

qa.q: A job with a specific date input crashes only on 29 February. Which technique reproduces it reliably?
qa.right: Controlling the clock in a test
qa.why: Injecting time lets date-dependent paths run on demand.

qa.q: An engineer wants to speed up a function because it looks slow. There are no measurements. What is wrong?
qa.right: The function may not be the bottleneck
qa.why: Measurement identifies where the time really goes.

qa.q: A DNS change was made yesterday but some users still reach the old server. Which tool shows the address a name resolves to?
qa.right: dig
qa.why: dig queries name resolution and shows cached or stale answers.

qa.q: Secure connections to an API failed on the same day every year with no code change. What should you check?
qa.right: The certificate expiry date
qa.why: Expired certificates cause sudden handshake failures.

qa.q: You need to see the requests a mobile app sends. What do you use?
qa.right: An intercepting proxy
qa.why: A proxy between app and server shows and can alter the traffic.

qa.q: Which breakpoint stops only on the thousandth item of a loop?
qa.right: A conditional breakpoint
qa.why: A condition prevents stopping on every iteration.

qa.q: A value in memory becomes corrupted and you do not know which line changes it. What helps?
qa.right: A watchpoint on that value
wrong: A stack trace of the login
qa.why: A watchpoint stops when the value changes.

qa.q: A native service crashed on a server where you cannot attach a debugger. What helps you analyse the crash?
qa.right: A core dump
qa.why: The memory image can be examined after the process has ended.

qa.q: Which is the right order when an outage begins?
qa.right: Restore service, then find the root cause, then write the postmortem
wrong: Find the root cause, then restore service
qa.why: Impact comes first.
